 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. Roman Reigns, Cody Rhodes and even John Cena — all of them can take a step back, as it looks like next weekend's Survivor Series has a new star attraction. The Rock is officially heading to Houston for his first WWE appearance since Elimination Chamber last year. As the man himself put it on Wednesday's "Pat McAfee Show": "The People's Champ is coming home."
 Naturally, the announcement has caused speculation to run wild — at least on certain corners of the internet — as to whether we could finally (no pun intended) be on the verge of that dream match between Roman Reigns and The Rock at next year's WrestleMania. After all, surely the gargantuan sums attached to SaudiMania would be too much to turn down, even for a Hollywood A-lister … right?
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Of course, we non-clickbaity types have a solemn duty to urge caution in these kinds of moments — not least given The Rock's effective estrangement from WWE, at least on a creative level, since last year. Then there's the fact that "The Final Boss" has some pretty demanding and lucrative engagements between now and then, including his return to the "Fast and Furious" franchise.
 So what could happen? Here is my assessment of the potential scenarios:
 A Hall of Fame announcement of some kind
 Even if The Rock isn't going to wrestle at SaudiMania, you can bet that all parties involved — whether that's Ari Emanuel or Turki Alalshikh — will still be moving heaven and Earth to get him there in some capacity.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement One suitably grand way to do that would be to involve The Rock in next year's Hall of Fame show. That might mean inducting him in his own right, or perhaps having him step forward as the guy who inducts John Cena, his old WrestleMania sparring partner. Of the two, I'd consider the latter to be marginally more likely.
 Given that the last few Hall of Fame ceremonies have been a little lacking in star power, confirming the involvement of The Rock — and potentially John Cena too — would be a smart way to make the build to SaudiMania feel extra special.
 Likelihood rating: 4 out of 5
 The Rock is returning to WWE, but whether "The Final Boss" has unfinished business with Roman Reigns or is simply stopping by remains to be seen.
 (WWE via Getty Images) Another cynical corporate cameo
 Cast your mind back to January 2025, when WWE made its much-hyped debut on Netflix, still riding high on the buzz from WrestleMania XL (when The Rock made his last in-ring appearance). When it was announced that "The Final Boss" would be appearing on the show, we all wondered whether we might be about to see the next chapter in the whole Rock/Cody/Roman saga.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Instead, we ended up with an anticlimactic, self-satisfied segment in which The Rock seemed to have forgotten all about 'Mania XL, instead opting to bury the hatchet with the guy he'd whipped into a bloody mess only nine months beforehand. Much of the speech felt like it was coming from TKO board member Dwayne Johnson, rather than his in-ring counterpart.
 While you'd hope they'd learned some lesson from that, I wouldn't rule out WWE giving us something similar next weekend. Given that this year's Survivor Series marks the 30th anniversary of Rocky Maivia's in-ring debut, there's a good chance we end up with a back-slapping segment to mark the occasion, thus helping boost viewing figures without any substantial payoff.
 Likelihood rating: 3 out of 5
 An actual Final Boss segment (but no 'Mania match)
 Given Dwayne Johnson's professed fondness for the whole "Final Boss" character, would there be some way he could at least do us the decency of making a kayfabe appearance — even if it turns out to be a one-and-done thing without any big commitments for 'Mania?
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement It certainly isn't impossible. With Roman Reigns now riding high again as WWE Champion, it would be easy to construct a believable segment where The Rock acknowledges his cousin in true Samoan style, thus further building up "The Tribal Chief" as the most dominant champion ahead of 'Mania 43.
 Likewise, there's potential to do something with Cody Rhodes, who also clearly has the respect of the real-life Dwayne Johnson. Perhaps The Rock could congratulate Cody on finally unleashing his ruthless streak at Crown Jewel. That would at least be congruent with the whole "Cody's soul" angle and would once again stoke the rumor mill about a potential Cody heel turn.
 Likelihood rating: 2.5 out of 5
 An incongruous comedy segment
 On the other hand, they could go the other way and opt for a crowd-pleasing comedy segment, similar to the John Cena skits from this year's WrestleMania. In other words, the sort of thing that gets a big pop in the moment from the slightly star-struck crowd, but which basically gets forgotten within 24 hours or so.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The good thing about a comedy segment (at least from WWE and Johnson's perspective) is that it can build toward The Rock actually doing a move or two, without any risk of injury. I saw a plausible-sounding scenario suggested on social media, where you have The Rock being interrupted by The Miz only for "The A-Lister" to eat another Rock Bottom for old time's sake.
 Likelihood rating: 2.5 out of 5
 The build to that WrestleMania match: Roman vs. Rock
 By now, we've all probably got the same kind of scenario in our head for how WarGames might end: An epic staredown between a triumphant Roman Reigns — having just led his tribe to victory against the 946 — and his elder statesman kayfabe cousin. After a few minutes of soaking up the moment, The Rock makes another of his famous hand gestures to indicate the game is on at 'Mania 43.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement As I've said, I don't think it's likely, but you'd be foolish to rule it out entirely. All the signs from the past 10 years indicate that — at least until recently — The Rock considered this to be the last million-dollar match on his wrestling résumé. Who knows, maybe he's had a visit from Maui in his dreams telling him that now really is the best time to make it happen.
 Again, it would be a surprise. But don't pretend you can't picture it happening. Dwayne Johnson making that fateful phone call to Ari Emanuel. "Hey Ari, let's tell Universal to hold the schedule for April … I'm in for Riyadh, brother."
 Likelihood rating: 1.5 out of 5
 The build to a different WrestleMania match
 Even if WWE can persuade The Rock to come out of semi-retirement, there's still one major issue with running Rock vs. Roman as next year's 'Mania main event. What would it mean for Oba Femi? Having bet the house on making "The Ruler" look like the next big thing, is WWE really going to make him pass his chance at destiny over to a part-timer twice his age?
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Of course, there is a compromise on that front. You could have The Rock wrestle elsewhere on the 'Mania card. That might involve setting up another double-header main event like they did at 'Mania XL — though good luck capturing that magic again — or maybe going down a totally different avenue altogether. Could they even put something in play for Cody vs. Rock maybe?
 Again, it's super unlikely. But if there was even a sliver of a chance of that happening, we'd probably get a clue next weekend.
 Likelihood rating: 1 out of 5
